question:
A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of worsening fever, headache, photophobia, and nausea for 2 days. One week ago, she returned from summer camp. She has received all age-appropriate immunizations. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F). She is oriented to person, place, and time. Physical examination shows a maculopapular rash. There is rigidity of the neck; forced flexion of the neck results in involuntary flexion of the knees and hips. Cerebrospinal fluid studies show:
Opening pressure 120 mm H2O
Appearance Clear
Protein 47 mg/dL
Glucose 68 mg/dL
White cell count 280/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 15%
Lymphocytes 85%
Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "13-year-old girl" -> "symptoms of fever, headache, photophobia, nausea" -> "recent return from summer camp" -> "maculopapular rash and neck rigidity" -> "CSF with lymphocytic predominance" -> "Echovirus as common cause of viral meningitis in children" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Neck rigidity and Brudzinski's sign" -> "indicates meningitis" -> "CSF shows lymphocytic predominance" -> "low to normal glucose levels" -> "Echovirus typically presents with these CSF findings in viral meningitis" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Fever, headache, photophobia, nausea" -> "maculopapular rash" -> "neck stiffness with positive Brudzinski’s sign" -> "CSF findings of lymphocytic predominance and normal glucose" -> "Herpes simplex virus usually causes encephalitis, not meningitis" -> "Echovirus more likely than Herpes simplex virus" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Recent summer camp attendance" -> "exposure to multiple pathogens" -> "symptoms and CSF findings suggest viral meningitis" -> "Echovirus common in communal settings like camps" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Maculopapular rash" -> "fever and signs of meningitis" -> "CSF with lymphocytic predominance and normal glucose" -> "Neisseria meningitidis typically shows elevated neutrophils, not lymphocytes" -> "Echovirus more consistent with CSF findings" -> 90%
analysis: The clinical presentation and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis suggest a diagnosis of viral meningitis, characterized by the presence of fever, headache, photophobia, nausea, neck stiffness, and a predominantly lymphocytic pleocytosis in the CSF. The CSF glucose level is normal, which is more typical of viral than bacterial meningitis. Echovirus, a member of the enterovirus family, is a common cause of viral meningitis, especially in children and adolescents returning from settings like summer camps where close contact facilitates virus transmission.
